key_insight: CVD-grown single-crystalline cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates exhibit robust anomalous Hall behavior, with calculations linking epitaxial strain to enhanced Berry-curvature-driven conductivity.
engineering_relevance: These non-layered ferromagnetic nanoplates offer a potential route to spintronic devices operating above room temperature.
method: CVD growth and structural characterization of epitaxial cubic Fe₃Ge nanoplates.
SQUID magnetometry, Hall transport measurements, and second-harmonic generation probing.
DFT calculations of strain-induced band reconstruction and anomalous Hall conductivity.
evidence_signal: Structural analysis indicates approximately 4.16% interfacial compressive strain, transport shows AHE persisting well above room temperature, and DFT predicts roughly doubled anomalous Hall conductivity consistent with experiment.
watch_item: Strain relaxes toward the surface, so controlling thickness and interface quality may be critical for reproducible device performance.
paper_title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge Nanoplates Grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition
